result.summary: The image shows a residential street with brick multi-family housing and a sidewalk on at least one side. The roadway is wide and lacks lane markings or designated pedestrian crossings, while the pavement surface shows significant cracking and degradation.

hazards.location_in_image: Entire visible roadway

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction

interventions.title: Pavement Resurfacing
interventions.description: Repair and resurface the roadway to eliminate cracks and provide a smooth, safe surface for all users.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalks and Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install high-visibility marked crosswalks and ADA-compliant curb ramps at intersections or mid-block locations to formalize pedestrian movements.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming Measures
interventions.description: Implement speed humps or curb extensions to reduce vehicle speeds on this wide residential street.

result.summary: The image shows a wide residential street lined with multi-story brick townhouses. Pedestrian infrastructure is incomplete, featuring a sidewalk on only one side and no marked crossings or traffic calming measures visible to manage the wide roadway.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossings
hazards.description: There are no painted crosswalks or signage indicating where pedestrians should cross the wide roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the main roadway in the foreground and midground.

hazards.name: Wide roadway width
hazards.description: The excessive width of the street may encourage higher vehicle speeds and increases the time pedestrians are exposed to traffic while crossing.
hazards.location_in_image: The entire visible span of the asphalt roadway.

hazards.name: Incomplete sidewalk network
hazards.description: The lack of a sidewalk on the left side of the street forces pedestrians to walk in the roadway or on private property.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the left side of the street in front of the townhouses.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks at intersections to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs at potential crossing points to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Completion
interventions.description: Construct a continuous paved sidewalk on the left side of the street to provide a safe, separated space for pedestrians.

result.summary: The image shows a residential intersection with sidewalks but a complete lack of pedestrian crossing infrastructure. There are no marked crosswalks, curb ramps, or traffic control signs visible to protect pedestrians crossing the street.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: There are no painted crosswalks at the intersection, making pedestrian movements less predictable to drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Intersection of Bergen Tr and the cross street.

hazards.name: Lack of Curb Ramps
hazards.description: The sidewalk ends at a vertical curb without a ramp, creating a barrier for people with mobility devices or strollers.
hazards.location_in_image: Corner of the sidewalk near the utility pole.

hazards.name: Uncontrolled Intersection
hazards.description: No stop signs or signals are visible to regulate vehicle right-of-way at the junction.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the intersection.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Paint continental or ladder style crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian space.

interventions.title: ADA Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install tactile, sloped curb ramps at all corners of the intersection to ensure accessibility.

interventions.title: Intersection Control
interventions.description: Install stop signs to manage traffic flow and improve safety for all road users at the junction.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a wide, unmarked residential intersection with significant gaps in the sidewalk network. The lack of formal crossing infrastructure and the presence of parked vehicles near corners create visibility and exposure risks for pedestrians.
